head: A calculator for
every pocket.
slides.sub: How Casio turned an office machine into something anyone could buy.

image.label: A small calculator on a 1970s Tokyo office desk
image.brief: 1970년대 도쿄 사무실 책상 위 작은 휴대용 계산기 하나. 따뜻한 오후 햇살, 주판과 서류가 옆에 놓임. 실제 로고나 제품 디자인은 따라 하지 않음.

head: Four brothers
and a relay machine.
body: In 1957, the Kashio brothers founded Casio in Tokyo. Their first product was an electric calculator built with relays, a large machine made for offices.
For years after, calculators stayed expensive tools that companies bought, not people.

image.label: A bulky office calculator in a 1950s workshop
image.brief: 1950년대 도쿄의 작은 작업장. 책상만 한 큰 사무용 계산기와 그 옆에서 작업하는 실루엣 인물들. 얼굴은 보이지 않게.

head: By 1970, everyone
was making calculators.
body: New chips made calculators smaller and cheaper. Dozens of Japanese firms rushed in, and prices kept falling in what became known as the calculator war.
Most still aimed at the same buyer: the office.

image.label: Crowded shelves of competing calculators in an electronics shop
image.brief: 1970년대 초 아키하바라풍 전자상가 진열대에 빽빽이 놓인 여러 회사의 계산기. 네온과 형광등 조명. 실제 브랜드 로고 없음.

head: Prices are falling fast.
What do you build?
body: You run a calculator maker in 1972. Rivals compete on features and size, and margins are shrinking.

options.text: Build a better office calculator with more functions
options.feedback: Offices would pay for it, but every rival was chasing the same buyers. Keep swiping.

options.text: Strip it to basics and price it for individuals
options.feedback: Fewer features means fewer office sales, and you need huge volume to profit. Keep swiping.

options.text: Leave calculators before the price war gets worse
options.feedback: Many firms did this. It protects cash but gives up a market that was still growing. Keep swiping.

image.label: A manager at a desk weighing two calculator prototypes
image.brief: 1972년 일본 사무실, 책상 위 두 가지 계산기 시제품을 바라보는 관리자의 뒷모습 실루엣.

slides.label: the price of the Casio Mini in 1972
body: Casio chose the basics. Most rival calculators cost several times as much. The Mini was priced so a student or office worker could buy one for themselves.

image.label: A price tag beside a small calculator in a shop window
image.brief: 1970년대 상점 쇼윈도에 놓인 작은 계산기와 손글씨 가격표. 거리의 사람들이 들여다보는 모습은 실루엣으로.

head: Less calculator.
More buyers.
body: Casio cut what most people did not need. The Mini showed six digits and did simple arithmetic, in a small, light case.
It was not the most powerful machine. It was the first one many people could own.

image.label: A simple calculator held in one hand
image.brief: 한 손에 쏙 들어오는 단순한 계산기. 버튼이 적고 숫자 표시창이 작게 빛남. 실제 제품 디자인은 그대로 따라 하지 않음.

slides.label: Casio Minis sold in about ten months, according to the company
body: Huge volume let Casio buy parts and build in larger runs, which pushed costs down further and made it hard for small rivals to keep up.

image.label: A factory line filled with small calculators
image.brief: 1970년대 일본 공장 조립 라인을 가득 메운 소형 계산기들. 작업복 입은 인물들은 뒷모습이나 실루엣으로.

head: The war ended.
Casio was still standing.
body: As prices kept falling, many makers left the business. Casio and a few large rivals remained.
The company went on to apply the same idea, simple and affordable electronics for individuals, to other products.

image.label: An empty factory beside a busy one
image.brief: 불 꺼진 빈 공장과 불 밝힌 바쁜 공장이 나란히 있는 대비 구도. 1970년대 일본 공업지대 분위기.

head: Don't fight for buyers.
Create new ones.
body: Rivals fought over offices. Casio made a calculator good enough for people who had never owned one, at a price they could pay.
A low price grew the market, and the volume made the low price profitable.

image.label: A small crowd of new users around a tiny device
image.brief: 작은 기기 하나를 중심으로 다양한 사람들의 실루엣이 둥글게 모인 그래픽. 학생, 주부, 직장인 느낌.

head: Look past your buyers
to the ones priced out.
body: The biggest market is often people who want what you sell but cannot afford or use it yet.
**Try it today:** who would buy your product if it were half the price and half the features? What would you cut?

image.label: A single calculator on a student's notebook
image.brief: 학생 공책 위에 놓인 작은 계산기 하나. 저녁 책상 조명, 1970년대 일본 가정 분위기.

factChecks.note: Casio Mini 출시(1972년 8월)와 가격 12,800엔은 Casio 공식 연혁 기준입니다. 출시 월을 다시 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1972년 12,800엔(경쟁품의 약 3분의 1) 확인.
"약 10개월 만에 100만 대 판매"는 Casio 발표 수치로 알려져 있습니다. 카드에 "according to the company"로 표시했고, 기간(10개월)을 공식 자료로 확인하세요. → [2026-11-02 확인] 출시 10개월 만에 100만 대 확인(Casio 공식).
Casio 창업(1957년, 가시오 4형제)과 첫 제품인 릴레이식 계산기 14-A는 Casio 공식 연혁 기준입니다. → [2026-11-02 확인] 1957년 릴레이식 14-A 확인.
당시 다른 계산기 가격은 구체적 수치 없이 "several times as much"로만 적었습니다. 1971~72년 휴대형 계산기 가격대(수만 엔)를 자료로 확인하세요.
Casio Mini의 6자리 표시창과 개인용 시장을 겨냥한 설계는 Casio 자료와 계산기 역사 자료 기준입니다. 6자리 표시 여부를 확인하세요.
일본 '계산기 전쟁'과 이후 많은 제조사가 철수한 일은 널리 기록된 사실이지만 업체 수는 자료마다 달라 숫자를 넣지 않았습니다.
